selected_source.title: Soldaat met speer te paard in een rivier (Soldier with spear on horseback in a river)
selected_source.creator: Jean Audran, after a painting by Charles Le Brun
selected_source.license: Public domain as stated in the Rijksmuseum object record

fit_rationale: The image supplies a single complete horse with readable body mass, hindquarters, lifted forelegs, hooves, and ground contact, plus one mounted rider in a forward-leaning action stance. The rider holds a long spear one-handed across the torso, giving unambiguous primitive ranged/melee action logic that can later be adapted into a sling, short javelin, or bone weapon. The complete horse silhouette and visible legs make this a strong rigging and proportion reference for Bone Riders.
adaptation_boundaries: Later adaptation may replace the spear with a one-handed sling or compact primitive ranged weapon and remove classical armor/helmet details.
Keep horse body, hind legs, lifted forelegs, rider seat, and forward action readable for later rigging; do not copy the print as a final model.
No identifiable living Indigenous regalia, sacred motif, culture-specific paint, or cultural authenticity claim is being carried forward.
rights_notes: The Rijksmuseum object record identifies the print, creator, date range, horse-and-rider subject, and explicitly lists Copyright: Public domain. The saved binary is the museum's IIIF image rendition associated with that object record.
uncertainty: The source is a nineteenth-century-style engraved rendition of a classical/early-modern military scene rather than a documentary depiction of Event 014's fictional group. Use pose, silhouette, horse anatomy, and one-handed weapon logic only; replace all culturally specific costume cues during adaptation.

processed_preview.method: Lossless decode to RGBA PNG; no crop, repaint, recolour, or background removal

dds_preview.method: Repository convert_to_dds.py; one-level uncompressed BGRA; evidence only, not a runtime texture

runtime_wiring: None; parent-owned model/entity wiring remains unchanged.
